A user reported: "We used Reducto and it did struggle with long documents." They process financial documents over 300 pages and say Gemini 3 Flash produces high-accuracy extracts very fast.

An Ask HN post sought high-quality alternatives to Reducto for document parsing. The poster needs strong table extraction and structured JSON output, says accuracy on messy PDFs is critical, and later added they want both high accuracy and high speed.

A user reported that the Reducto Studio launch link (links.reducto.ai/studio) didn't work and returned ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS. A second user said it was still not working after the team said it was fixed.
A user reported that the Reducto mobile website was broken. It crashed with "a problem repeatedly occurred" on both Safari and Chrome on their iPhone, and they suspected an infinite loop.
A user complained that Reducto's pricing page offered a data processing agreement only on the enterprise plan, noting a DPA is a legal requirement for any European company.

A non-customer praised the detailed design of Reducto's website, including the typography, layout, line-work and textured gradients. Another commenter liked that it wasn't another Tailwind template and especially loved the illustrations and icons.

Asked how Reducto compares with Datalab on accuracy, one commenter complained that many document extraction companies leave out benchmarks that include Marker. Another user wanted to test Reducto side by side with Datalab and their own pipeline.
A user who had chatted with the team months earlier said Reducto Studio "looks like a great UX." Another said they were already considering the Reducto API and would try Studio.
